# <span id="aanchor165"></span> Message Description Editor

Accessing this form requires **Application Process - FLOWCAL Options** privileges.

Messages form an organized audit trail of changes made to FLOWCAL settings, device creation and deletion, and process status changes.

Four types of messages are generated:

- System
- Location
- Meter
- Source

All messages can be viewed and acknowledged from the Message Viewer. Messages can also be configured for automatic notification by email. Use the Message Description Editor to view and edit the default configuration for a message, specifically the message class and priority, and to designate email notification recipients.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Message Description Editor:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.
2.  Select **Message Description** within the **Application** group.
3.  Select the **System**, **Location**, **Meter**, or **Source** radio button to filter the grid by message type.
4.  Select a message and click **Edit**.
5.  Edit the class and priority designation as needed.
6.  Click **Save**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 661;height: 495;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Message Description Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Message Description Editor screen:

- **Number** - Unique numeric identifier for the message.

- **Class** - User defined for the client’s needs depending on their IT and business structure. The class level defined for the message; Class levels are Error, Warning, Information, and Security. Where a warning could be a normal exception, whereas an Error could be a critical exception.

- **Priority** - Severity classification for events that have occurred.

  - **0** - Messages that are not to be written. Setting the priority level to zero will disable the message for the entire application.
  - **1–10** - Messages that are to be written with an initial status of "Logged".
  - **\> 10** - Messages that are to be written with an initial status of "Unacknowledged". These messages can then be acknowledged; "Logged" messages cannot.

  The Priority setting is application-wide and requires services to be restarted.

- **Message** - The message description. This should only be altered for clarification; changing the description will not alter the underlying meaning or the way the message is generated.

- **Data Usage** - Data points populated for the message selected. These can vary by message.

- **Contact Name/D-List** - Existing contacts or distribution lists defined for each message (designated in the Notify field). The contacts specified will receive an email when the message is generated.
